item.title: Trump's AI action plan: US president signs executive orders; seeks to make America leader in artificial intelligence race
item.description: Donald Trump signed executive orders to reshape America's AI landscape, targeting 'woke' AI and streamlining data center permits. He aims to make the US an AI export powerhouse, emphasizing the need to win the AI race against other nations. The orders include an action plan to accelerate AI adoption and boost American AI exports, replacing previous Biden-era regulations.

item.title: Trump vs Columbia: Ivy league school to pay $200 million in landmark settlement; campus protests curbed
item.description: Columbia University will pay over $220 million and implement policy changes to settle allegations of civil rights violations concerning the protection of Jewish students. The agreement with the Trump administration includes federal oversight, independent monitoring of admissions and hiring, and dismantling discriminatory programs.

item.title: WSJ claims Trump was told in May that his name was in Epstein Files multiple times, White House says 'fake news'
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported that Attorney General Pam Bondi informed President Trump in May that his name appeared in Epstein documents. The report also mentioned other high-profile figures were named, with files containing unverified hearsay. The White House dismissed this report as fake news.

item.title: UAE confirms new school year dates for 2025–2026: Key changes every parent should know
item.description: The UAE has introduced a unified school calendar for the 2025–2026 academic year, applicable to all public and private schools. Approved by the Education Council, the calendar sets standardised dates for term starts, holidays, and breaks. It includes mid-term holidays to ease academic pressure and aligns with the ‘Year of Community’ goals of supporting family and social cohesion.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: H-1B wage levels: What will change in the new US immigration rules that will end visa lottery?
item.description: The US administration plans to overhaul the H-1B visa selection process, prioritizing wage levels over the current lottery system. This shift, welcomed by US tech workers, aims to prevent companies from hiring lower-skilled foreign workers at reduced wages. International graduates looking for entry-level jobs in America will suffer as they will not get a chance in the proposed system.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE unveils new university academic calendar for 2025–2026: What students need to know
item.description: The UAE’s Ministry of Higher Education has released a revised academic calendar for 2025–2026, aligning university schedules across public and private institutions. The new structure balances academic needs with student wellbeing, synchronizes holidays with schools, and allows limited flexibility. It reflects a broader push to make higher education more responsive to community values and institutional requirements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Democrat congressman Greg Casar introduces bill to ban AI-driven price; seeks Republican support
item.description: US Congressman Greg Casar has introduced the Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025, aiming to curb AI-driven price discrimination. The bill targets companies exploiting personal data to charge varying prices, a practice the FTC has also flagged. It further seeks to prevent AI from determining wages based on personal finances.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New warning for green card holders in US: Always carry THIS at all times with you, CBP reminds
item.description: Customs and Border Protection reminded green card holders to carry proof of alien registration, as required by law. Failure to do so may result in a misdemeanor and fines. This reminder, under the Trump administration, signals continued strict enforcement, emphasizing that lawful permanent residents are not exempt from legal consequences, including potential deportation for violating laws.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030: Five years left, how much progress has been made and will it succeed?
item.description: Saudi Arabia is undergoing a significant transformation with Vision 2030. The plan aims to diversify the economy beyond oil. It focuses on tourism, technology, and clean energy. Social reforms are underway, offering more opportunities for young Saudis and women. Mega-projects like NEOM are attracting global attention. The initiative seeks to improve the quality of life and attract foreign investment.

item.title: Relentless bullying: Emmanuel Macron sues Candace Owens for claiming French First Lady was born a man
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Brigitte Macron have initiated legal action against Candace Owens in a Delaware court, alleging defamation. Owens is accused of spreading false claims that Brigitte Macron was born male, using these claims to boost her platform and profits through an eight-part podcast series.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US announces investigation into Harvard's use of international visas, gives one-week deadline for details
item.description: The Trump administration has initiated a new investigation into Harvard University's use of international visas, marking the third aggressive action against the institution. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the inquiry into Harvard's Exchange Visitor Program, demanding university records and potential interviews with staff and visa holders.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Search on for missing Wisconsin grad student: Eliotte Heinz last seen walking alone
item.description: La Crosse authorities are seeking public assistance in locating Eliotte Heinz, a 22-year-old Viterbo University graduate student, missing since early Sunday. Last seen walking from Broncos Bar around 3:30 am towards her apartment, she never arrived home. Police are utilizing multiple resources and requesting residents to check home camera footage from 2 am to 6 am.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bryan Kohberger sentence updates: Families of Idaho victims address 'soulless' killer directly; 'You were that foolish'
item.description: Bryan Kohberger faced the victims' families during a sentencing hearing, where emotional impact statements were delivered. Steve Goncalves, father of Kaylee Goncalves, confronted Kohberger, detailing the evidence that quickly led to his identification as the murderer of the four University of Idaho students. "You were that foolish, that careless, that stupid," he said.

item.title: Canada dad arrested on charges of daughter's murder in US cheated on wife; almost lost one eye in an assault in Ethiopia
item.description: Luciano Frattolin, the 45-year-old father arrested in the US on charges of killing his daughter, is a prominent businessman in Ethiopia. His former friends revealed dark details of his past, how he was assaulted in 2019 that made him lose his one eye, and how he cheated on his wife when he was recovering from the attack in Ethiopia, leading to their divorce.
